Hi Tessa - great call earlier. Thanks for walking us through the current priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Stakeholders we heard on the call:
- Tessa Morgan - Champion / Product Owner (primary contact)
- Christine Valdez - Economic buyer (CFO) - needs topline ROI and procurement cadence
- Alan Chen - Procurement (procurement@finovate.com) - will own vendor evaluation
- Security team - SOC 2 / data residency review (you mentioned a security questionnaire)

Decision criteria you highlighted:
- Predictable unit economics (per-token + predictable monthly commit)
- Latency (sub-300ms p95 target on common flows)
- Security & compliance (SOC2, audit logs, optional VPC/private deployment)
- Ease of integration (Chat & embeddings API, SDKs)

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send a one-pager ROI summary and a short champion talk-track you can use with Christine. (Attached: Redwood_ROI_onepager.pdf)
2) Rishi (cc'd) will send a security packet / answers to RFI items and a brief tech talk-track for your engineers. (We can attach a security packet zip.)
3) Tessa - can you confirm procurement timelines? You mentioned vendor selection target of early October. If that's correct, can you introduce Christine (CFO) and Alan (procurement) on a short call next week for SOW/pricing alignment?
4) We can run a 30-min enablement session for your champion + procurement + security so everyone has the same talking points. Proposed windows: Mon/Tue next week, late morning PST.

Please flag anything I missed. If you're good with the ask-to-introduce to Christine, I'll prepare the one-pager and a short 10-slide deck excerpt for that meeting.

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

Best,

Champion enablement talk track (use as email/snippet to Christine):

- "We ensure predictable monthly costs with Dedicated capacity or commit tiers, plus observability to watch unit economics at route level."

Q: What SLAs/backstop for latency?
A: We target <300ms p95 for common flows; Dedicated pools give tighter guarantees and higher SLOs.
